title: Signs on the page
summary: Read slurs, staccato dots, accents, pauses, repeat marks and metronome marks.
usSummary: Read slurs, staccato dots, accents, fermatas, repeat marks and metronome marks.

hook.text: Glide across the floor and every step melts into the next. Now tiptoe: step, stop, step, stop. Music has both. Press play: every note here runs straight into the next. How would the same tune sound if it tiptoed?

explore.text: Play the five highlighted keys, C up to G. First make them glide: hold each key until the next one starts, so the notes join. Then make them tiptoe: lift your finger at once, so there is a gap after every note.
explore.goal: Play the five keys joined up, then again with a gap after every note.

cards.text: Smooth and joined, with no gaps, is [[legato|legato]]. A curved line over notes of different pitches, a [[slur|slur]], asks for it. A [[tie|tie]] looks similar but joins two notes of the *same* pitch into one long sound. Short and detached is [[staccato|staccato]]: a small dot above or below the note.

An [[accent|accent]] is a sideways V: play that note with extra force. A [[pause|pause]] is a dot under an arch: hold the note longer than written. [[cantabile|Cantabile]] means in a singing style; [[dolce|dolce]] means sweet and soft. A [[metronome-mark|metronome mark]] such as ♩ = 80 gives the speed: 80 beats a minute.

A double [[bar-line|bar line]] with dots means play that section again: these are [[repeat-marks|repeat marks]]. [[da-capo|Da capo]] (*D.C.*) means go back to the beginning. [[dal-segno|Dal segno]] (*D.S.*) means go back to the sign, a curly S with a slash and two dots. [[fine|Fine]] is the end, and [[al-fine|al fine]] means play on to Fine.

alternative.text: Think of gliding and tiptoeing: [[legato|legato]] glides, [[staccato|staccato]] tiptoes. Now think of a journey. [[repeat-marks|Repeat marks]] send you round the loop again. *D.C. al fine* says: drive back to the start, then stop at the sign that says [[fine|Fine]]. A [[pause|pause]] is a red light: wait there, then carry on.

questions.prompt: Listen to both clips. Which one is **staccato**?
questions.hint: Staccato is short and detached. Listen between the notes: which clip has silence after every note?

options.reason: Clip A runs each note straight into the next: that is [[legato|legato]]. [[staccato|Staccato]] has a gap after every note, as in clip B.

questions.prompt: Match each sign to its name.
questions.hint: One sign is a curve, one is a dot and one is a sideways V.

face.text: A curved line over notes of different pitches

left.reason: A curved line over notes of different pitches is a [[slur|slur]]: play them smoothly, as [[legato|legato]].

face.text: A small dot above or below a note

left.reason: A small dot above or below a note asks for [[staccato|staccato]]: short and detached.

face.text: A sideways V above a note

left.reason: A sideways V is an [[accent|accent]]: play that note with extra force.

questions.prompt: Two notes of the **same** pitch are joined by a curved line. What is it?
questions.hint: Look at the pitches. Which curved line joins different pitches, and which joins matching ones?

options.reason: A [[slur|slur]] joins notes of different pitches. Two notes of the same pitch joined into one long sound make a [[tie|tie]].
An [[accent|accent]] is a sideways V above a note, not a curved line. Matching pitches joined by a curve are a [[tie|tie]].

♩ = 72 is a [[metronome-mark|metronome mark]]: it says how many beats to play each minute.

questions.prompt: Which word asks you to play **in a singing style**?
questions.hint: Imagine a singer shaping a long, flowing line.

options.reason: [[dolce|Dolce]] means sweet and soft. A singing style is [[cantabile|cantabile]].
[[staccato|Staccato]] is short and detached, which is not how singers shape a line. A singing style is [[cantabile|cantabile]].

questions.prompt: Listen to both clips. Which one is **legato**?
questions.hint: Legato is smooth and joined. Which clip has no gaps between the notes?

options.reason: Clip B has a gap after every note: that is [[staccato|staccato]]. [[legato|Legato]] is smooth, with no gaps, as in clip A.

questions.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.hint: Two are about how notes join. Two are about the feel of the music.

left.reason: [[legato|Legato]] means smooth and connected, with no gaps.
[[staccato|Staccato]] means short and detached, with a gap after each note.

questions.prompt: A curved line joins two notes of **different** pitches. What is it?
questions.hint: A tie joins matching pitches. What joins different ones?

options.reason: A [[tie|tie]] joins notes of the same pitch. Different pitches joined by a curve are a [[slur|slur]].
An [[accent|accent]] is a sideways V, not a curved line. Different pitches joined by a curve are a [[slur|slur]].

questions.prompt: What does *D.C.* tell you to do?
questions.hint: Da capo is Italian. Capo means head: where is the head of a piece?

options.reason: That is *D.S.*, [[dal-segno|dal segno]]. *D.C.* is [[da-capo|da capo]]: back to the very beginning.
Stopping is what [[fine|Fine]] marks. *D.C.* does the opposite: it sends you back to the beginning.

questions.prompt: Listen to both clips. Which one is **staccato**?
questions.hint: Listen between the notes. Which clip leaves a gap after each one?

options.reason: Clip B runs each note into the next: that is [[legato|legato]]. [[staccato|Staccato]] leaves a gap after every note, as in clip A.

questions.prompt: A piece ends with *D.C. al fine*. Put what you play in order.
questions.hint: Da capo sends you back to the beginning. Fine tells you where to stop.

face.text: Play from the start to the *D.C.*

payload.reason: *D.C. al fine*: play to the *D.C.*, go back to the start, then play on until *Fine* and stop.

questions.prompt: What does a [[pause|pause]] over a note ask you to do?
questions.hint: A [[pause|pause]] is an arch with a dot under it. Think of what the name suggests.

options.reason: Playing louder is what an [[accent|accent]] asks for. A [[pause|pause]] is about length: hold the note on.
Short and detached is [[staccato|staccato]]. A [[pause|pause]] asks you to hold the note longer, not cut it short.

questions.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.hint: Two words send you back. Two are about the end.

left.reason: [[da-capo|Da capo]] means go back to the beginning.
[[dal-segno|Dal segno]] means go back to the sign.
[[fine|Fine]] marks the end, where the piece stops.
[[al-fine|Al fine]] means play on until you reach Fine.

questions.hint: It is a metronome mark. A metronome counts in minutes.

options.reason: A [[metronome-mark|metronome mark]] does not count repeats. Repeat marks do that. The number says how many beats fit in a minute.
Loudness is shown by signs such as *f*. The number in a [[metronome-mark|metronome mark]] is a speed: beats every minute.

questions.prompt: What does an accent ask for?
questions.hint: An accent is a sideways V. Think of a word you say with extra stress.

options.reason: Holding a note longer is what a [[pause|pause]] asks for. An [[accent|accent]] asks for extra force.
Short and detached is [[staccato|staccato]], shown by a dot. An [[accent|accent]] asks for extra force.

[[cantabile|Cantabile]] means in a singing style. Sweet and soft is [[dolce|dolce]].

points: [[legato|Legato]] is smooth and joined; a [[slur|slur]] joins notes of different pitches. A [[tie|tie]] joins two notes of the same pitch into one long sound. [[staccato|Staccato]] is short and detached.
An [[accent|accent]] means extra force. A [[pause|pause]] means hold the note longer. [[cantabile|Cantabile]] is singing and [[dolce|dolce]] is sweet and soft.
[[repeat-marks|Repeat marks]] mean play again. [[da-capo|Da capo]] goes back to the beginning, [[dal-segno|dal segno]] to the sign, and [[al-fine|al fine]] plays on to [[fine|Fine]].
A [[metronome-mark|metronome mark]] such as ♩ = 80 says how many beats to play each minute.
